articles.title: Tiger that mauled British man to death won't be euthanized, zoo says
articles.summary: A tiger that killed a man who entered its enclosure at a British zoo over the weekend will not be euthanized, park officials said Sunday.
articles.body:
Oct. 11 (UPI) -- A British zoo where a man was mauled to death by a tiger over the weekend said Sunday it will not euthanize the animal.

The tiger, named Altai, will not be put to death after the incident in which police said the man was killed after entering the big cat's enclosure at the Yorkshire Wildlife Park in Doncaster, England.

"We would like to thank everyone who has expressed their concern following yesterday's tragic incident," the zoo said in a social media statement issued Sunday. "Our thoughts and heartfelt sympathies remain with the family and loved ones of the man who sadly lost his life."

Park officials said the facility would remain closed to give its staff time to recover from the incident.

"Many, many people have contacted us about Altai, the tiger," they added. "We can reassure everyone that he is safe and well and will not be euthanized as a result of this incident."

South Yorkshire Police said they received reports of a man entering Altai's enclosure at 1:35 p.m. local time on Saturday.

"The tiger subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injury," they said in a statement . "Emergency services attended and sadly, despite the best efforts of medical personnel, the man was pronounced dead at the scene."

Altai was uninjured and remained in the enclosure following the incident, posing no wider risk to the public, police said.

"I'm deeply saddened to hear of the incident at Yorkshire Wildlife Park," said Ed Miliband, the British foreign secretary and member of Parliament for the Doncaster area.

"I send my thoughts and deepest condolences to the family of the individual who died. I am very grateful to the emergency services and staff of the park who responded," he said in a Facebook post .

articles.title: Lotofácil: Grupo de apostas ganha quase R$ 900 mil em Itumbiara | G1
articles.standfirst: Sargento organizou bolão com 25 cotas em sua própria lotérica em Itumbiara e faturou mais de R$ 860 mil na Lotofácil. Cada participante vai receber cerca de R$ 34 mil com o bilhete premiado.
articles.summary: Organizado por sargento em Itumbiara, bolão da Lotofácil com 25 cotas fatura R$ 866 mil e garante prêmio individual de R$ 34 mil aos participantes.
articles.body:
Sargento Glaciel Andrade organiza o grupo de apostas há 14 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal Glaciel

O grupo de apostas organizado pelo sargento Glaciel Andrade, conhecido pelas apostas milionárias, acertou o prêmio principal da Lotofácil e faturou R$ 866.955,89 . De acordo com o apostador, foram 25 participantes no bolão e, dessa vez, o grupo acertou uma aposta de 14 e outra de 15 dezenas sorteadas no concurso 3802.

Glaciel é dono de uma lotérica em Itumbiara , no sul do estado. O concurso que premiou o grupo de amigos foi sorteado neste domingo (11). Ele disse ao g1 que foram feitos três jogos de 17 números, totalizando 25 cotas, com cada cota levando o prêmio de R$ 34.678,24. "Acertamos o prêmio principal da Lotofácil ontem", comemorou .

Os números sorteados foram: 02 - 03 - 05 - 06 - 09 - 10 - 11 - 12 - 14 - 15 - 19 - 20 - 21 - 23 - 24 .

De acordo com Glaciel, em 2025 o grupo acertou os 15 pontos na Lotofácil da Independência e faturou R$ 4,9 milhões. Ele afirmou que o bolão está em forte expansão e que, só em 2026, já são mais de 7 mil cartelas premiadas na lotérica Pé Quente que, segundo ele, é a número um de Goiás em vendas de bolões, acertos e premiações.

"Esse bolão nosso é o bolão que a gente joga já há 14 anos. Começou com um bolão de amigos, no ano passado, na mega sena da virada, nós jogamos cerca de R$ 13 milhões e dessa vez nós acertamos", comemora.

Para jogar na Lotofácil, o apostador precisa escolher entre 15 e 20 números no volante. Há ainda duas outras modalidades: a Surpresinha, em que o sistema escolhe os números para o apostador, e na modalidade Teimosinha, quando o apostador pode concorrer com os mesmos números por até 24 sorteios consecutivos.

A aposta mínima custa R$ 3,50 e as premiações acontecem a partir dos 11 acertos.

articles.title: Rio Branco vacinou mais de 30 mil crianças até outubro de 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Imunização de rotina abrange faixa etária de zero a 12 anos. Doses pendentes podem ser conferidas na caderneta de vacinação.
articles.summary: Imunização de rotina abrange faixa etária de zero a 12 anos. Doses pendentes podem ser conferidas na caderneta de vacinação.
articles.body:
O município de Rio Branco já aplicou vacinas em 30.058 crianças entre janeiro e outubro deste ano. É o que aponta a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde (Semsa), nesta segunda-feira (12). Os imunizantes aplicados são os considerados de rotina, como contra o sarampo , meningite e febre amarela , que abrange a faixa etária de zero a 12 anos.

Além da imunização, serviços para acompanhar o crescimento e o desenvolvimento infantil também são mantidos. Segundo a Semsa, foram feitos mais de 49 mil atendimentos com cirurgião-dentista e quase 27 mil consultas com profissionais de enfermagem, superando os resultados registrados em 2025.

👉 O governo do estado confirmou, na última quinta-feira (8), dois casos de sarampo em pacientes residentes no Peru que foram atendidos em Rio Branco . Segundo a Sesacre, os pacientes são uma criança de 11 meses e uma mulher de 30 anos, moradores de Puerto Maldonado, no Peru. O último caso de sarampo registrado no Acre havia sido em 2000, segundo a pasta.

Rio Branco vacinou mais de 30 mil crianças até outubro de 2026, diz Saúde — Foto: Asscom/Semsa Rio Branco

Ao longo de dez meses, a Atenção Primária à Saúde contabilizou 41.035 consultas médicas , enquanto os serviços especializados computaram 1.212 consultas médicas.

A pasta detalha ainda que foram registradas 1.276 triagens neonatais, procedimento que ajuda a identificar, de forma precoce, possíveis alterações de saúde nos recém-nascidos.

Conforme a pasta, o resultado reforça a importância de manter a vacinação em dia. Por isso, as famílias são orientadas a procurar uma unidade de saúde para verificar a caderneta de vacinação e atualizar as doses pendentes, com a aplicação de acordo com a idade e previstas no calendário vacinal.

De acordo com o secretário de Saúde de Rio Branco, Rennan Biths, o objetivo é ampliar o acesso à vacinação na capital.

“Nosso trabalho é vacinar, prevenir e proteger. [...] Amplia o acesso aos serviços e orienta os pais sobre a importância de manter a caderneta de vacinação atualizada. Seguimos trabalhando para prevenir doenças, fortalecer a assistência e cuidar da saúde de nossas crianças”, afirmou.

articles.title: Previsão do tempo Uberlândia e região: calor e chuva até 100 mm | G1
articles.standfirst: Temperaturas devem ficar de 1°C a 3°C acima da média entre 12 e 18 de outubro. Pancadas de chuva devem acontecer em pontos isolados, em distribuição irregular.
articles.summary: A previsão do tempo para Uberlândia e região indica calor até 3°C acima da média e chuvas irregulares com risco de raios e ventos entre 12 e 18 de outubro.
articles.body:
Pancadas de chuva isoladas estão previstas para Uberlândia — Foto: Adreana Oliveira/g1

A semana de 12 a 18 de outubro será marcada por temperaturas acima da média climatológica e pancadas de chuva irregulares no Triângulo Mineiro e Alto Paranaíba. A previsão indica que os termômetros podem ficar de 1°C a 3°C acima do esperado para o período , enquanto os acumulados de chuva podem variar de 30 a 100 milímetros em diferentes setores das duas regiões, com volumes maiores em pontos isolados.

A tendência foi apontada pelo geógrafo William Borges, com base em modelos meteorológicos do Centro Europeu de Previsões Meteorológicas de Médio Prazo (ECMWF). Segundo a análise, as chuvas não devem atingir todos os municípios da mesma forma, e algumas localidades podem registrar pouca precipitação ao longo da semana.

Em Uberlândia , Uberaba , Prata e Tupaciguara, a tendência é de calor acima da média, com períodos de sol e aumento da nebulosidade. Há possibilidade de pancadas de chuva, principalmente nos momentos de maior instabilidade atmosférica.

No oeste do Triângulo Mineiro, em cidades como Ituiutaba , Santa Vitória, Frutal e Campina Verde, o aquecimento pode ser mais intenso durante as tardes. Já em Araxá , Patrocínio e Patos de Minas , no Alto Paranaíba, as temperaturas podem ser relativamente menores por causa da altitude, embora também devam ficar acima do padrão climatológico.

Chuva pode vir acompanhada de raios e rajadas de vento

A combinação entre calor e umidade na atmosfera pode favorecer a formação de nuvens carregadas. Com isso, há possibilidade de pancadas de chuva acompanhadas de descargas elétricas e rajadas de vento, além de precipitações intensas em períodos curtos.

Apesar da possibilidade de volumes expressivos em alguns pontos, os modelos não indicam um cenário generalizado de chuva acima da média em toda a região. A distribuição irregular significa que municípios próximos podem registrar acumulados bastante diferentes.

A estimativa de 30 a 100 milímetros é regional e não representa uma previsão específica para cada cidade. Além disso, a análise não permite confirmar a ocorrência de tempestades severas.

Umidade do ar pode cair durante as tardes

Nos períodos sem chuva, o calor pode contribuir para a redução da umidade relativa do ar, principalmente durante as tardes. Nas localidades atingidas pelas pancadas, os índices de umidade podem aumentar temporariamente.

A tendência é de alternância entre períodos de sol, calor, aumento da nebulosidade e chuva. Como se trata de uma previsão semanal, a localização e a intensidade das precipitações podem mudar conforme as próximas atualizações dos modelos meteorológicos.

articles.title: Quaest no DF: como está a disputa pela presidência no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta segunda-feira (12) é a primeira encomendada pela Globo à Quaest no segundo turno. Margem de erro é de três pontos percentuais.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta segunda-feira (12) é a primeira encomendada à Quaest pela Globo no 2º turno. A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT), que disputam o segundo turno presidencial no dia 25 de outubro. — Foto: Wilton Junior/Estadão Conteúdo e Diego Herculano/Reuters

Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta segunda-feira (12) mostra como está a disputa presidencial no Distrito Federal para o segundo turno nas eleições de outubro.

Esta é a primeira rodada da pesquisa desde que o segundo turno entre Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula foi confirmado , no último domingo (4).

O segundo turno será em 25 de outubro. Na data, eleitores do DF também decidem a eleição para governador, entre Celina Leão (PP) e Leandro Grass .

Veja abaixo os números da pesquisa estimulada, em que a Quaest mostra aos eleitores entrevistados os nomes dos candidatos:

Quaest, 12 de outubro: intenção de voto para presidente no 2º turno no DF — Foto: Arte/g1

Para 94% dos eleitores ouvidos no levantamento, a escolha do candidato é definitiva. Outros 6% dizem que ainda podem mudar o voto até o segundo turno.

A Quaest ouviu 1.104 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 8 e 11 de outubro . A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais , para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95% . O número de registro da pesquisa é BR-06799/2026.

A pesquisa divulgada nesta segunda (12) também mediu a aprovação do trabalho de Lula como presidente.

articles.title: Região de Piracicaba tem 14 das 18 cidades sem Delegacia da Mulher | G1
articles.standfirst: Unidades são especializadas no atendimento a mulheres vítimas de violência e na investigação de crimes relacionados à violência de gênero.
articles.summary: Unidades são especializadas no atendimento a mulheres vítimas de violência e na investigação de crimes relacionados à violência de gênero.
articles.body:
A região de Piracicaba (SP) tem a grande maioria das cidades sem Delegacias de Defesa da Mulher (DDMs). Dos 18 municípios da área de cobertura do g1 Piracicaba , 14 não possuem a delegacia especializada.

As unidades são especializadas no atendimento a mulheres vítimas de violência e na investigação de crimes relacionados à violência de gênero.

Segundo dados do Governo de São Paulo, os municípios que não têm DDMs são:

Por outro lado, Piracicaba, Limeira (SP), Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP) e Capivari (SP) contam com esse tipo de delegacia.

Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher de Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/ EPTV

A falta de delegacias especializadas pode criar obstáculos para mulheres que tentam denunciar situações de violência doméstica. Foi o que aconteceu com uma moradora de Nova Odessa (SP), que precisou procurar atendimento em outra cidade após ser agredida pelo marido.

No dia seguinte à agressão, ela decidiu registrar um boletim de ocorrência, mas descobriu que não havia Delegacia da Mulher na cidade. Por isso, procurou atendimento em Sumaré (SP) e precisou se deslocar novamente, desta vez até Americana (SP), para realizar o exame de corpo de delito.

"Eu ainda tive um meio de transporte, porque eu tenho carro, para chegar lá. E a mulher que não tem?", questionou a vítima, que preferiu não ser identificada.

Ela conseguiu registrar a ocorrência e obter uma medida protetiva, mas avalia que a necessidade de viajar para outros municípios pode desestimular mulheres que já enfrentam dificuldades para denunciar.

"Se tivesse uma DDM aqui, como Nova Odessa já é um município pequeno, de repente a pessoa consegue ir à pé, ou consegue um Uber que fica mais em conta para ir aqui pertinho. Mas, para se deslocar até Sumaré ou Americana, eu acho que dificulta um pouco mais", afirmou.

Quase 80% das cidades paulistas não têm DDM

No estado de São Paulo, 514 dos 645 municípios (79,7%) não possuem delegacia especializada, segundo o governo estadual.

Na área de cobertura da EPTV , que inclui 49 municípios das regiões de Campinas e Piracicaba, a proporção é de 67,3%, com 33 cidades sem DDM.

Outro desafio é o horário de funcionamento. Em toda a área de cobertura da EPTV, apenas as delegacias da mulher de Campinas e Piracicaba funcionam 24 horas por dia.

Nas demais cidades que possuem o serviço, as vítimas precisam considerar os horários de atendimento das unidades ou recorrer a outras delegacias fora do expediente.

A Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SSP) informou que, desde 2023, a rede especializada foi ampliada em mais de 87% no estado, passando de 202 para 379 unidades, entre DDMs e Salas DDM.

De acordo com a SSP, o atendimento 24 horas também vem sendo ampliado. Atualmente, 39 DDMs contam com funcionamento integral, e a previsão é de alcançar 58 unidades até o fim de 2026.

"Nos municípios que não contam com DDM física, as demais unidades da Polícia Civil estão aptas a atender mulheres vítimas de violência e registrar ocorrências. O atendimento também pode ser realizado 24 horas pela DDM Online e pelo aplicativo SP Mulher Segura", complementou.

articles.title: Apoiadores de Lula fazem ato em Copacabana, na Zona Sul do Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Apoiadores ocuparam vários quarteirões da Avenida Atlântica, em Copacabana; estações de metrô da Zona Sul registraram grande movimentação.
articles.summary: Às 13h, a mobilização se concentrava na altura do posto 5, entre as ruas Barão de Ipanema e Xavier da Silveira.
articles.body:
Um ato em apoio ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), candidato à reeleição, reunia eleitores na Avenida Atlântica, em Copacabana, na Zona Sul do Rio, no início da tarde desta segunda-feira (12).

Por volta das 13h, os apoiadores estavam concentrados na altura do Posto 5, entre as ruas Barão de Ipanema e Xavier da Silveira. Meia hora depois, o grupo se espalhava por cerca de sete quarteirões da Avenida Atlântica.

A movimentação também era intensa no transporte público, com lotação nas estações de metrô Cantagalo, Siqueira Campos e Botafogo.

Em um momento do ato, o cantor e compositor Gilberto Gil apareceu na sacada de um prédio e foi aplaudido.

Apoiadores de Lula fazem ato em Copacabana, na Zona Sul do Rio — Foto: GloboNews

Neste domingo (11), Lula participou de um ato na Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, que reuniu aliados, apoiadores e lideranças políticas. Ao discursar, defendeu que seus eleitores conversem com pessoas que deixaram de votar no primeiro turno.

Na quarta-feira (7), estudantes também fizeram um ato no Centro do Rio em uma mobilização, chamada de “Juventude na Rua pela Democracia”, que teve concentração na Candelária e caminhou até a Cinelândia.

À tarde, outro ato popular reuniu apoiadores do presidente Lula na Lapa, no Centro do Rio. Por volta das 16h, já era possível ver vários grupos de manifestantes no bairro.

O ato na Lapa foi convocado por sambistas e representantes da cultura popular do Rio e foi batizado como "O samba não se cala – a luta é na rua". A mobilização reúne nomes de destaque do carnaval carioca em uma demonstração de apoio ao candidato do PT.

articles.title: Papa cancela audiências até 20 de outubro por cirurgia  | G1
articles.standfirst: Pontífice anunciou no domingo (11) que médicos detectaram um nódulo em seu pulmão. Vaticano não informou nem se nódulo é benigno ou maligno, nem se viagem que papa tem para a América Latina em novembro será mantida.
articles.summary: Pontífice anunciou no domingo (11) que médicos detectaram um nódulo em seu pulmão. Vaticano não informou nem se nódulo é benigno ou maligno, nem se viagem que papa tem para a América Latina em novembro será mantida.
articles.body:
Jornalistas aguardamem frente à Basílica de São Pedro, no Vaticano, em 12 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Yara Nardi/ Reuters

O papa Leão XIV cancelou todas as audiências que tinha previstas ao longo desta semana em decorrência da cirurgia à que será submetido nesta terça-feira (13). A operação será feita para a retirada de um nódulo no pulmão.

O Vaticano informou que a agenda do pontífice até 20 de outubro foi toda cancelada . Mais cedo, o porta-voz do Vaticano havia confirmado que Leão XIV será internado na terça no hospital Gemmeli, em Roma.

➡️ No domingo (11), o pontífice anunciou que médicos detectaram um nódulo em seu pulmão "em estágio inicial" e recomendaram a cirurgia. No anúncio, feito a fiéis durante oração na Praça São Pedro, Leão XIV disse que operação ocorreria nos "próximos dias".

O Vaticano não especificou se ele manterá ou não a viagem que tem programada para a América Latina no mês que vem. No domingo, o porta-voz do Vaticano, Matteo Bruni, disse apenas que a recuperação da cirurgia durará cerca de uma semana .

O papa Leão XIV anunciou no domingo que médicos detectaram um nódulo em estágio inicial em seu pulmão . O pontífice afirmou que será submetido a uma cirurgia nos próximos dias. Leão XIV, de 71 anos, fez o anúncio diretamente a fiéis durante oração dominical na Praça de São Pedro, no Vaticano.

O pontífice afirmou que o nódulo foi detectado em estágio inicial e seu crescimento está "bem controlado" . Ainda assim, afirmou o papa, médicos recomendaram a cirurgia para a remoção .

“Queridos amigos, durante alguns exames médicos recentes, os médicos encontraram um nódulo localizado em meu pulmão. Ele foi detectado em um estágio muito inicial e está bem localizado. Os médicos consideram a cirurgia adequada. Seguindo a orientação deles, decidi, portanto, submeter-me a uma operação para removê-lo. A cirurgia já está agendada para os próximos dias. Agradeço pela proximidade espiritual de vocês e confio-me às suas orações", disse o papa aos fiéis.

➡️ Um nódulo pulmonar é uma massa densa encontrada no pulmão. A maioria dos nódulos detectados em exames, sem estar associados a sintomas, costuma ser benigna .

O porta-voz do Vaticano, Matteo Bruni, não deu detalhes do exame . Bruni disse apenas que a cirurgia ocorrerá daqui a alguns dias, no hospital Gemelli, em Roma, e que recuperação do pontífice após a cirurgia deverá levar cerca de uma semana.

Papa Leão XIV durante oração dominical — Foto: Filippo Monteforte / AFP

O porta-voz também não informou se o pontífice seguirá com a sua agenda depois disso -- Leão XIV tem uma viagem de duas semanas no início de novembro para a América Latina , a primeira que fará ao continente. Pela previsão, ele visitará Uruguai, Argentina e Peru, país que viveu por mais de 20 anos.

No Angelus, a oração deste domingo na qual o pontífice fez o anúncio, ele fez referência à viagem, agradecendo a fiéis por orações "pela viagem pastoral que eu farei" .

Também não havia informações, até a última atualização desta reportagem, sobre o atual estado do pontífice, que tem 71 anos e não apresenta nenhum outro problema de saúde conhecido. Ele costuma se exercitar durante a semana, segundo o Vaticano. O pontífice faz natação e joga tênis .

De origem norte-americana, Robert Prevost foi eleito papa em maio de 2025, substituindo o papa Francisco, argentino, que morreu em abril do ano passado após uma série de problemas de saúde.

articles.title: Google Maps starts showing live fuel prices across UK, to be powered by UK government's Fuel Finder scheme
articles.summary: Drivers across United Kingdom (UK) can now check real-time gas station prices on Google Maps.
articles.body: Drivers across United Kingdom (UK) can now check real-time gas station prices on Google Maps. This comes after the UK government announced partnership with search giant Google. AS per the release, drivers are set to save at the pump as near real-time petrol and diesel prices now appear on Google Maps. To checking local fuel prices, users need to open Google Maps and search for a forecourt nearby, with near real time prices for petrol and diesel displayed on the app.As per the official release, this marks the latest step in the government’s work to tackle the affordability crisis, after the VAT cut to electricity bills and a £2 cap on bus fares, giving families some breathing space with the cost of living.Minister for Energy Consumers Polly Billington said, "Tackling the affordability crisis is our first responsibility and for so many families and businesses, petrol and diesel are essential goods, not luxuries. Accessing the cheapest fuel should be simple, which is why it is a gamechanger for near real-time fuel prices to be shown on Google Maps for the first time in the UK, helping drivers to find the best deal and save money at the pump."Chancellor of the Exchequer, John Healey, said, "Getting the best price at the pump is now easier. This doesn’t fix everything; bills have gone up because of events in the Middle East. But we’re not powerless. And small changes like this, cutting tax on electricity bills and capping bus fares at £2 all help give families a bit of breathing space."What is UK government's Fuel Finder schemeUK Government claims that Fuel Finder scheme was created to help drivers get more competitive fuel prices following a recommendation by the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA). It added that an overwhelming majority of petrol stations are inputting data to Fuel Finder promptly, with around 99% of all fuel sold on UK roads now reflected.Since February, it has been compulsory for petrol stations across the UK to report the price of their fuel within 30 minutes of it changing or risk a fine – and the CMA can take action where there is evidence that petrol stations are not complying with the law.The data is already used by thousands of drivers across apps such as Waze, Petrol Prices, the AA, Confused.com and RAC Fuel Watch, and its integration with Google Maps will help millions more motorists find the best price at the pump.Sarah-Jayne Williams, Director of Global Product Partnerships for Geo at Google, said, "Navigating fuel rising costs shouldn’t add stress to everyday journeys. Integrating Fuel Finder data into Google Maps and Waze gives drivers visibility on nearby pump prices, helping drivers make intentional choices to help their budgets go further this winter."You use AI every day. articles.title: A Connecticut town paid $455,000 for a historic two-family home to create about 20 library parking spaces; a state preservation council has now voted to ask the attorney general to stop its demolition
articles.summary: A plan to demolish a historic house in Manchester, Connecticut, to make space for additional library parking has faced opposition from the state's
articles.body: A plan to demolish a historic house in Manchester, Connecticut, to make space for additional library parking has faced opposition from the state's Historic Preservation Council. The town purchased the two-family property for $455,000 in June 2026, intending to replace it with around 20 parking spaces. However, preservation officials have now voted to seek intervention from the state's attorney general to prevent the demolition, according to CT Insider.The property, located at 29-31 Eldridge Street, stands next to Manchester's new Main Street library. It is part of the Cheney Brothers Historic District, an area recognised as a National Historic Landmark in 1978. The house was originally built to accommodate workers employed at the Cheney Brothers silk mills.The town's decision to demolish the building drew objections from some residents and members of the local historical society. Their concerns ultimately led to a review by Connecticut's Historic Preservation Office.On Wednesday, the Historic Preservation Council unanimously voted to ask the attorney general to intervene under the Connecticut Environmental Protection Act. The law allows action against the 'unreasonable destruction' of protected resources. Although commonly used to protect natural resources, it can also be applied to historic buildings.House can be restoredDuring the council meeting, preservation advocates argued that the property should be repaired rather than demolished.According to Brad Schide, a member of Preservation Connecticut, restoring the house would be a more appropriate solution. “The structure should be rehabbed and maintained in its present configuration. That to us is the prudent and feasible alternative,” Schide said.Dave Goslin, a principal at Krosky Architects, also assessed the building. Goslin, whose firm handles preservation projects, rated its quality eight out of 10. He said the house had remained in relatively good condition considering its age, although renovations were necessary.“When it was built it was well built and it has held up pretty well over time. The conditions within the building are tired. It’s in need of renovations,” Goslin said.Goslin suggested that Manchester could sell the property to a developer interested in historic preservation. Such a buyer could restore the building and continue using it as a two-family residence.He also proposed another option that would allow the town to create some parking without removing the house. Under this plan, the garage would be demolished to make room for approximately 10 parking spaces. However, Goslin acknowledged that the arrangement would leave the property with a 'substandard' lot and effectively turn its backyard into a parking area.Why town wants to demolish?Manchester officials maintained that the house was in poor condition and that keeping it would create additional maintenance costs.Town Manager Steve Stephanou described the property as an eyesore and defended the proposed demolition. “We cannot afford to operate and maintain a structure that frankly has been blighted for some time,” Stephanou said.He added that the building had not been properly maintained over the years and that vehicles had previously been parked on its lawn.According to Stephanou, the new library already has 54 parking spaces included in its plans. The town expects parking demand to increase, and the additional 20 spaces could eventually be reserved for library employees. He also argued that removing the building would eliminate a blind spot at the rear of the parking lot.Concerns over historic districtPreservation advocates raised concerns beyond the future of this particular house. Schide warned that demolishing one historic property could encourage the removal of others in the neighbourhood.“We find it all the time. Buildings, as they are removed, it kind of encourages other removal. If there’s too much of that you lose everything," Schide said.He noted that Eldridge Street still retains much of its historic character and that preserving the house would help protect the wider district.Stephanou responded that Manchester had no intention of demolishing other historic buildings. He said the town would even sign an agreement preventing further removals.However, Andy Horowitz, a Historic Preservation Council member and the state historian, argued that the district's National Historic Landmark designation already provided a basis for protecting its buildings. “It’s hard to argue here unambiguously that it’s beyond repair,” Horowitz said. He maintained that the existing historic designation should be sufficient reason to oppose demolition.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: David Beckham’s UNICEF 7 Fund supported 406,400 children; its four-country projects reached their final year in 2024
articles.summary: When David Beckham launched 7: The David Beckham UNICEF Fund in February 2015, he set out to help protect vulnerable children and give them a better
articles.body: When David Beckham launched 7: The David Beckham UNICEF Fund in February 2015, he set out to help protect vulnerable children and give them a better chance of reaching their potential. The initiative went on to support work addressing violence, bullying, child marriage and barriers to education, particularly among girls. Its projects in Nepal, Indonesia, Uganda and El Salvador worked with schools, families, communities and governments to strengthen child protection and improve access to education. UNICEF UK’s 2024 annual report described that year as the final year for the fund’s then-current projects. The programme’s reported results offer a picture of what the initiative achieved, while also raising an important question: whether the systems and services strengthened through the projects can sustain those gains after the funded work ends.David Beckham’s 7 Fund for UNICEF: how the initiative developedUNICEF and Beckham announced the fund on 9 February 2015. It was designed to raise money and awareness for children facing violence, abuse, disease and barriers to education, with particular attention to those most at risk. The initiative was named after Beckham’s familiar shirt number and formed part of his commitment to use his public profile to support UNICEF’s work. UNICEF announced support for work in Nepal, Indonesia, Uganda and El Salvador in 2018, although its 2024 annual report describes the current four-country programme as having operated since 2019. El Salvador had also featured in the fund’s original 2015 launch. Beckham visited Indonesia in 2018 to meet children and learn about bullying and violence affecting their education.They addressed different problems according to local needs, from child marriage and school exclusion in Nepal to bullying in Indonesia and violence affecting children in Uganda and El Salvador. Rather than focusing only on immediate assistance, the programmes worked with schools, families and community organisations to strengthen protection systems and help children remain in or return to education. The distinction between the fund’s launch and its later projects matters when assessing its record. UNICEF UK’s 2024 annual report said the four-country projects had reached their final year and reported that the fund had supported 406,400 children. That milestone does not mean the wider fund or Beckham’s relationship with UNICEF ended in 2024. It means the specific programme described in those four countries had reached the end of its planned project period.Nepal and Uganda: supporting girls’ education and preventing violenceIn Nepal, the fund supported programmes in Madhesh Province, where child marriage and barriers to education can prevent girls from continuing their studies. According to UNICEF UK’s annual report, 21,723 girls who were out of school completed the Supporting Adolescent Girls’ Education programme. The nine-month initiative provided literacy and numeracy instruction to help participants enrol in formal schooling and continue their education. The report also said more than 50,000 children and adolescents received information and support relating to mental health and the harmful effects of child marriage. The fund also supported Rupantaran, a life skills programme intended to help adolescents build confidence and make informed decisions. One participant, Antima, was profiled by UNICEF as a girl from a large family who had left school because her family could not afford to keep her enrolled. She began selling snacks and now earns about NPR 700 a day, helping support her family and pay for her younger siblings’ education, according to the 7 Fund’s account. Her story illustrates the financial pressures that can contribute to school exclusion, although an individual account cannot establish how typical such outcomes are.The 7 Fund’s Uganda project page reports that more than 25,000 adolescents in Adjumani District participated in life skills sessions, although its headline gives a lower overall figure of more than 23,000 children reached through life skills programmes. More than 10,400 parents and caregivers received information about violence prevention and harmful practices that can affect school attendance and completion. The programme also supported teacher training and systems for tracking and reporting violence in schools. UNICEF has profiled young people who used life skills clubs as a route back into education and towards careers they hoped to pursue. Christine Manuela, for example, was reported to have begun nursing and midwifery training at Kuluva Hospital in Arua District after participating in a Girls Education Club supported by the fund.Indonesia and El Salvador: tackling bullying and creating safer spacesIn Indonesia, the fund supported efforts to address bullying and peer violence, which can make school an unsafe environment and disrupt children’s education. Beckham visited the country in March 2018, meeting children involved in anti-bullying initiatives. UNICEF reported that the programme encouraged students to speak up when they experienced or witnessed violence and to help create safer learning environments. The 7 Fund’s project account says more than 147,500 adolescents in Indonesia participated in polls about bullying and mental health. These consultations gave young people an opportunity to express their views on issues affecting them. The programme also sought to involve schools and local authorities in improving children’s safety. Such participation figures measure engagement with the initiative; they do not, by themselves, establish how much bullying declined or how many children stayed in school as a direct result.In El Salvador, the programme focused on child protection and safe places for children to learn, play and take part in community activities. It worked in municipalities including San Marcos and San Martín, supporting child protection services and efforts to make public spaces more suitable for children. The 7 Fund’s project page reports that more than 1,600 child protection workers and community leaders received training and that more than 28,500 children took part in sports and recreational activities in safer community spaces. UNICEF UK’s 2024 annual report gives a different figure for recreational activities, reporting more than 27,300 children, and says 41,351 children and adolescents benefited from the programme overall. These figures refer to different reported measures and should not be treated as interchangeable. The approach recognised that children’s safety depends on more than what happens in classrooms. Access to trusted adults, community services and safe places to spend time can also matter, particularly in areas affected by violence and social disadvantage. However, the number of people trained or children using these spaces should be understood as programme reach, rather than proof on its own that violence has fallen across the communities involved.You use AI every day. articles.title: Woman who bought a £10 ring at a London flea market and wore it for decades saw its 26.27-carat diamond sell for £656,750
articles.summary: Imagine slipping a cheap, grubby cocktail ring onto your finger, wearing it regularly for many long decades, and never suspecting that it hides a fortune.
articles.body: Imagine slipping a cheap, grubby cocktail ring onto your finger, wearing it regularly for many long decades, and never suspecting that it hides a fortune. That is precisely what happened to one woman, who paid just ten pounds for a dull-looking ring at a West London car boot sale, which Americans call a flea market. Thirty years later, a local jeweller's glance, a detailed laboratory report and a frenzied London bidding room transformed her bargain into a viral story that made international headlines. This article explains where the ring came from, what experts discovered, and why such a find is possible.How a £10 bargain at a West London car boot sale in Isleworth led to an unexpected diamond discoveryIn the late 1980s, according to Sotheby's, a woman was browsing a car boot sale in Isleworth, West London, when a box of costume jewellery caught her eye. She was drawn to some bangles, and paid little attention to a cocktail ring holding a single clear stone. Sigee writes that the ring sat in a rusty old setting and looked dull and filthy, nothing special at all. The seller wanted twelve pounds for the whole lot, and the buyer haggled the price down to ten pounds. The bangles and the ring went home with her. The Guardian, reporting through the Press Association, confirms that the ring was bought in the 1980s and that its owner believed it was a decorative costume jewel.Why the ring looked worthless for thirty years and how a local jeweller suspected a genuine diamondFor three decades the ring was simply an everyday piece of jewellery. Sotheby's reports that its owner wore it regularly, as anyone might wear a cocktail ring, convinced it could not be worth anything. Only in 2017 did she take it to a local jeweller, who immediately sensed something special. He suspected a genuine diamond but found it too large to measure accurately, so she telephoned Sotheby's. Jessica Wyndham, Sotheby's Head of High Jewelry in Europe, told Sigee that few people imagine they are carrying a stone of such size, adding that "if you've always believed something isn't valuable, there's little reason to question it." Wyndham also explained that the mount, a blend of silver and gold typical of the late nineteenth century, tarnished over time, leaving it darker and duller than modern settings.What the Gemological Institute of America report revealed about the 26.27 carat cushion cut diamondSotheby's sent the piece to the Gemological Institute of America for evaluation, and Sigee reports that the verdict was striking. The cushion-cut diamond weighs 26.27 carats, carries a colour grade of I and earns an impressive clarity grade of very, very slightly included, level two. The Guardian, in its Press Association report, adds that the stone is thought to have been cut in the nineteenth century, although its history and how it arrived at the Sotheby's sale remain unknown. The older cuts were fashioned to display fire, the splitting of light into spectral colours, whereas modern diamonds are cut to maximise brilliance. She said these proportions give a distinctive personality that collectors now find especially appealing. She added that on first seeing the diamond in person, it was clear the stone was special.How the bidding at the sale pushed the Tenner diamond to £656,750After the diamond was confirmed as genuine, the story went viral and made international headlines. The Guardian reports that the sale took place in London and that the stone was snapped up for close to twice that figure, at £656,750, a life-changing sum for its owner according to Sigee. Wyndham said, in comments carried by the Press Association, that it was a thrill to bring the hammer down on two much-discussed objects and see that attention turn into strong bidding competition. The second object was a Cartier diamond brooch worn by Margaret Thatcher, which achieved £81,250 against an estimate of £25,000 to £35,000, with proceeds going to the Endeavour Fund, a charity supporting wounded, injured and sick servicemen and women.What the Tenner diamond teaches collectors about checking old jewelleryThe story also carries practical lessons. Sotheby's has handled jewels found hidden in old curtains, tucked into chair upholstery and uncovered beneath floorboards in forgotten garages, though she stressed that the Tenner diamond is remarkable for its size, quality and extraordinary circumstances. For anyone inspired to search a relative's jewellery box, she recommended looking for signatures in the mounts or stamps on the pieces themselves, which are the clearest clues to when an item was made, who made it and its level of quality. Sigee adds that every Sotheby's jewellery specialist is a gemologist who can identify the key characteristics of gemstones. The diamond's former owner still attends car boot sales regularly, knowing treasures may hide in unlikely places.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Anti-CEC protest: Congress chief Kharge dons Batman mask during march to Supreme Court
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge was seen donning a Batman mask on Monday while marching towards the Supreme Court to file a plea against poll
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge was seen donning a Batman mask on Monday while marching towards the Supreme Court to file a plea against poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar.Kharge, who was sitting next to Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, wore the superhero mask, which has become a trend in protests taking place around the world.However, this was not the first time the Congress had come up with the idea of using Batman for its political messaging.In August, posters portraying Rahul Gandhi as the “real-life Batman” was put up outside the Congress headquarters in Delhi.The posters feature the message, “The silent guardian, a watchful protector. LoP Rahul Gandhi, the real life batman.”Earlier this month, Rahul Gandhi launched an “Ask Me Anything” session inviting young people to question him on topics ranging from student protests and education to politics and philosophy. Announcing the initiative on X, Gandhi wrote, “Students, Gen-Z -- I'm here to listen."Ask me anything on Instagram, and I'll answer as many questions as I can.” One of the questions asked, “Are you Batman?” Gandhi appeared to play along with the long-running social media meme comparing him to the fictional superhero.“Let’s just say that no one has ever seen me and Batman in the same room together,” Rahul replied.Opposition stalwarts, along with hundreds of supporters and activists, undertook their "March for Democracy" to the Supreme Court on Monday on a heavily barricaded route and filed a joint petition against SIR and alleged poll irregularities, in another show of strength after a series of street protests over the "vote chori" charge.Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee, CPI's D Raja, CPI-M leader M A Baby, RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, besides NCP-SCP leader Supriya Sule, were among those who joined the march.A day after the Chief Justice of India (CJI) declined a request for a meeting with the LoPs on the issue, saying the matter is sub judice, the opposition leaders filed the joint plea in the apex court over alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The opposition leaders had said they wanted to hand over a memorandum to the CJI demanding an end to vote chori, Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, halting of the SIR of electoral rolls and switching back to the paper ballot format.As police stopped the march at Bhagwan Dass Road, several leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Tejashwi Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav, climbed atop a vehicle and the procession moved forward after crossing the barricades, as supporters cheered and waved flags.In a charged atmosphere, leaders and their supporters raised slogans against the government, CEC Kumar and asserted that "vote chori" and SIR exercise would not be allowed.A large number of supporters had already reached the Barakhamba Road junction at Connaught Place, from where they marched a few kilometres towards the Supreme Court with Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra leading the protesters along with AISA chief Neha Bora.Shiv Sena-UBT leader Sanjay Raut, CPI-ML leader Dipankar Bhattacharya and IUML leader E T Mohammed Basheer were among those present, besides Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar, Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy (all from Congress).Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Deadly gold mine air strikes highlight Egypt-Sudan border insecurity
articles.summary: Deadly air raids on gold miners in Sudan expose deepening border lawlessness and regional instability.
articles.body:
An alleged air strike on a gold mining site in northern Sudan has killed at least 72 workers , according to a rights group, highlighting the severe security vacuum along the country’s increasingly lawless border with Egypt.

The Khartoum-based rights group Emergency Lawyers accused the Egyptian military of targeting civilian miners in the North Wadi area of Jabal al-Uqaydat, a mountainous border area between Sudan and Egypt.

Egypt has not commented on the incident.

Images allegedly from the site and shared by rights monitors showed chaotic scenes, with bodies wrapped in funeral shrouds.

The border region between Sudan and Egypt has a long history of tensions which continue to this day.

In 1899, the British and Egyptian governments designated the 22nd parallel north as the dividing boundary between Sudan and Egypt on maps.

But the absence of physical border demarcation along this line, coupled with the area’s gold wealth, has left the area open to dispute and lawlessness.

Abdul Kareem Al-Almin Ahmed, a specialist in Egypt-Sudan border affairs, said the Sudanese territorial borders have long been subject to historical negligence which still goes on.

“The presence of the Egyptian Border Guard forces near the region, amid a complete lack of Sudanese military or administrative presence, has left the Sudanese highly vulnerable to Egyptian violations and encroachment,” he told Al Jazeera.

“What is required now from the Sudanese state – if it exists – is to elevate and escalate this issue to the United Nations as an encroachment on Sudanese territory. This must be followed by the immediate physical demarcation of border points in this region and along the entire border strip, in addition to establishing border observation posts along the entirety of the borders.”

In June, another artisan gold mine in the Jabal al-Uqaydat region was targeted by drones and artillery, with a number of people killed. The Egyptian army said it carried out an operation “within Egyptian territory” and detained 223 people.

Egyptian security forces continue to conduct sweeps of the border to combat what they described as illegal migration, drug smuggling and illegal mining.

Egypt and Sudan have a long history of border tensions stretching back to the colonial period which goes beyond the Jabal al-Uqaydat area.

The Halaib Triangle, a 20,580sq km area on the African coast of the Red Sea, has been a flashpoint between Egypt and Sudan for over a century.

The dispute stems from conflicting colonial-era maps. An 1899 agreement between Britain and Egypt regarding Sudan and parts of Libya placed the triangle within Egyptian political boundaries. But a 1902 British administrative decree handed control to Khartoum because the area was closer to the Sudanese capital.

The triangle, home to the Bisharin tribe, is renowned for its fertile lands and rich mineral deposits, including uranium, granite, copper and gold.

Following clashes between the two militaries on the border in the 1990s, Sudanese forces withdrew from the area in 2000 and Cairo has maintained effective control over the territory since.

The latest unrest follows the start of the civil war in Sudan in April 2023, which has pitted the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), allegedly backed by Egypt, against the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

The conflict has devastated the country and collapsed the economy. Abject poverty has forced many into dangerous methods of gold mining, including unregulated mines on the border. The collapse of central authority in Sudan has also allowed lawlessness to flourish in the borderlands.

Sudan’s gold has been a key source of financing for both sides, but there is no indication that the gold mine revenue in the border region is going to either party in the war.

Osama Ahmed Eidrous, a professor of strategic and security studies, told Al Jazeera that foreign powers have prolonged the conflict between the two sides.

“What is happening in Sudan is not a civil war; despite the presence of the Rapid Support Forces as one of the fighting parties in this war, this war is a war of external aggression within a large regional project,” Eidrous said.

“Everything that is happening in Sudan now in terms of effects on the Sudanese citizen, the weakness of the central government and the difficulty of controlling the borders, all these things are caused by this ongoing war in Sudan.”

He added that the miners posed no threat to neighbouring countries, such as Egypt, and were not involved in the war.

“We are talking about miners working in gold mining and we have not heard that there was an armed clash, or that they were carrying weapons, or that they were fighting the Egyptian government or the Sudanese government,” he said.

“They are Sudanese citizen miners who were suddenly attacked by the Egyptian aviation and struck for the second time, killing 85 of them.”

articles.title: Aberfan 60th anniversary to see royal visit from King, Queen and Prince William
articles.summary: The tragedy saw 116 children and 28 adults killed when a colliery spoil tip collapsed in 1966.
articles.body:
The King, Queen and Prince of Wales are set to visit Aberfan later this month to mark the 60th anniversary of the disaster which killed 116 children and 28 adults.

Pantglas Junior School and surrounding houses in the village near Merthyr Tydfil, south Wales, were catastrophically engulfed in coal slurry after the colliery spoil tip collapsed on 21 October 1966.

King Charles III, Queen Camilla and Prince William will join survivors, bereaved parents and members of the community on the anniversary to pay tribute to those who died.

The royals will visit the Aberfan Memorial Garden which stands on the site of the primary school, and go to the Aberfan and Merthyr Vale Community Centre.

Late Queen Elizabeth II's reaction to the disaster in Aberfan was said to be one of the biggest regrets of her 70-year reign.

A short prayer and a moment of silence will be held in the memorial garden, and King Charles and Prince William will lay wreaths. Queen Camilla will place a posy in memory of those who were lost.

During the visit to the community centre they will meet retired emergency service workers who helped respond to the coal tip collapse, including a 96-year-old woman who was a police officer at the time.

They will also look at an exhibition that shows the huge scale of the rescue effort.

As part of their visit, the royals will spend time with former Pantglas Junior School pupils, siblings of those who died and members of the Aberfan Wives, a support group established for mothers who lost children in the disaster.

The village's Ynysowen Male Voice Choir, which formed in the aftermath of the disaster and became a support group for local men to share their experiences, will also perform.

Personal reflections will be shared from survivors and family members in the community hall, including from Jeff Edwards, who survived the disaster as an eight-year-old pupil.

Prince William will visit Ynysowen Community Primary School - which was established to carry forward the legacy of Pantglas Junior School - to unveil an Aberfan Memorial Tree.

It aims to provide a permanent place for children, families and visitors to remember the victims and reflect on the lasting impact of the tragedy.

The tree was designed and created by ArtMetal, a family-run metalwork company based in Rhayader, Powys.

The concept was developed by Ynysowen Community Primary School headteacher Simone Roden, along with Edwards who is vice chair of governors at the school.

During the early planning stages, pupils helped shape the vision of the memorial by sharing drawings and ideas.

While Prince Philip, Lord Snowdon and the then prime minister Harold Wilson visited the scene of the disaster the following day, the Queen waited eight days before going to the village, arriving to comfort the community shortly after a mass funeral had taken place.

Her former private secretary, the late Lord Charteris, previously said he felt he had given her poor advice to "stay away until the preliminary shock had worn off".

He added at the time it was the biggest regret of her reign.

But for those left mourning, there was nothing but love and respect for the Queen, who they felt helped them during their darkest hour.

In total she returned four times after her first visit during her reign, including to open Ynysowen Community Primary School in 2012.

articles.title: Beginning in 1938, Raymond Isidore covered his Chartres home, chapel and garden with broken plates and glass; decades later, his mosaic world became Maison Picassiette
articles.summary: Explore La Maison Picassiette in Chartres, a stunning museum created by Raymond Isidore from broken plates and glass, showcasing his unique mosaic art. Learn about its transformation from a personal project to a national historical monument.
articles.body: A cemetery worker spent decades turning a modest home in Chartres into a mosaic environment made out of broken crockery, porcelain and glass, according to the Ville de Chartres. What began with a few pieces collected from fields and rubbish repositories became La Maison Picassiette, now a museum owned by the City of Chartres and recognised as a national Historical Monument. Isidore was born in Chartres on September 8, 1900, the seventh of eight children in a modest family of the era. He received a basic education and moved through several jobs, from being a foundry moulder to a railway employee and municipal theatre prop man. He joined the City of Chartres as a road worker in 1935, and later worked as a sweeper at Saint-Chéron cemetery, where he remained until resigning in 1958.How a modest house became a mosaic Isidore purchased a plot on Rue du Repos in 1929 and built a three-room house with help from his stepsons Michel and Bernard Rolland. It had a kitchen-dining room, a small living room and a bedroom, and decoration was not originally planned. That changed when he encountered broken pieces during a walk in 1938 and began collecting, sorting and storing the fragments in his garden. The work expanded across the interior, with the walls, floors and ceilings covered in mosaics. Furniture and everyday objects, including a bed, kitchen table, sewing machine and chair, also became part of the composition. In the painted areas, he added flowers, birds, landscapes and other scenes to surfaces that were not covered with fragments.Isidore’s designs were guided partly by dreams such as the patterns, people and buildings he later depicted appeared to him in this way. His imagery included an array of Christian symbols, animals, biblical scenes, Jerusalem and views of cathedrals, including Chartres Cathedral. He travelled for miles in search of debris, gathering discarded crockery and glass from dumps; eventually, his neighbours gave him the nickname Picassiette, a French term for a scrounger that also echoes Picasso and plates, according to Spaces Archives.From private creation to public landmark The project eventually expanded beyond the house itself and by 1945, Isidore had begun decorating the exterior, including an enclosure wall, while later work extended across gates, pathways and the garden. In 1956, he undertook new construction behind the house, including a chapel and summer house, and bought an adjoining plot for further garden decoration. These spaces allowed his imagery to become more expansive.The chapel is filled with Christian scenes and symbols, including a large cross and a nativity scene, alongside a countryside scene with a woman, shepherd, dog, chickens, rabbits and ploughs. One wall depicts cathedrals and places of worship using black glass and white china; another includes Jerusalem, the Leaning Tower of Pisa and the Colosseum. In addition to the mosaic representations of cities and notable buildings featured in the summer house, Isidore placed a throne at the base of the elaborate exterior composition.Isidore continued working right up until his death in 1964, and in 1962, he built the Tomb of the Spirit, which stands as his final achievement. The City of Chartres acquired the property in 1981, and it was given national Historical Monument status in November 1983. The Maison Picassiette is now a public museum, preserving the one-man mosaic world built over decades.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: PC thought murderer was making 'empty threats' before arson attack
articles.summary: PC Gemma Quinn did not think it necessary to arrest Zak Bolland after Michelle Pearson's 999 call.
articles.body:
A police officer called to the home of a mother and four children hours before they were murdered in an arson attack has told an inquest she thought the killer was making "empty threats".

PC Gemma Quinn told Bolton Coroner's Court she did not think it necessary to arrest Zak Bolland "there and then" after Michelle Pearson made a 999 call saying the 26-year-old had threatened her son and her home on Jackson Street in Walkden, Salford.

Four of Michelle's children were murdered in the arson attack on 11 December 2017. Michelle, 37, died in August 2019, after being badly burned.

Quinn, a Greater Manchester Police (GMP) officer of 14 years, told the court she planned to arrest Bolland when she was next on shift two days later.

"I carry the guilt every day," she said. "Never in my wildest dreams did I think this would happen."

A tearful Quinn said: "I have not done front-line policing since."

Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, Lia, three, died at their Walkden home in December 2017.

Bolland and David Worrall were jailed for life in 2018 for the murder of the four children, and in 2021 were also convicted of Michelle's murder.

Bolland was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 40 years and Worrall was sentenced to life with a minimum of 37 years in jail.

An inquest began on 5 October to examine the contact Michelle had with police and social services in the weeks leading up to the fire.

The court heard Quinn and PC Mike Grundy went to the scene in Walkden around 01:25 GMT after Michelle Pearson called 999 because Bolland and three others were outside her house.

Bolland had been heard shouting "I'm going to break Kyle's jaw" and threatened to "boot the door down".

Quinn, as the senior officer, told the court she knew Bolland, two weeks earlier, had threatened to set fire to Michelle Pearson's house and smashed windows with a hammer.

There were also markers on databases about his drug use, firearms and violence.

Yet she chose not to arrest Bolland as she believed it was an "empty threat".

"As a police officer, you get to see the worst side of a community and unfortunately, Salford and what I saw in 14 years….individuals make threats like that, quite often."

Her shift was not due to end until 05:00, the inquest heard.

Bolland's last known address was close by, but Quinn chose to go back to the police station.

When asked whether she should have tried to arrest him immediately, Quinn said "In hindsight, yes".

She told the court: "It's not that we had stopped dealing with the job, we had write-ups to do.

The family's barrister, Anna Morris KC asked if that work was more important than questioning Bolland - to which Quinn replied: "No".

Quinn said: "As a police officer, you get to see the worst side of a community and unfortunately in Salford and what I saw in 14 years, individuals make threats like that quite often.

"We didn't believe we needed to make an arrest, there and then, that night."

In his statement, Grundy had told Michelle he expected Bolland to be arrested.

It was suggested in the inquest that this was likely to have made Michelle feel she was not in any danger.

The inquest also heard that despite asking Michelle if she felt safe in the house, she sought not to try and move the family immediately to a secure location.

Quinn said she did not see the point in calling Michelle's housing provider, City West, because it was out of hours.

articles.title: Katie Price tells ex's rape trial allegations 'really shocked' her
articles.summary: Price tells court she was "really shocked" to learn of allegations against ex-husband Kieran Hayler.
articles.body:
Katie Price says she believed a teenage girl who was allegedly raped by her ex-husband was "afraid" after exchanging text messages with her, and that she was "really shocked" to learn of the allegations.

Price's ex-husband Kieran Hayler is on trial accused of three counts of rape and one of sexual assault against the then 13-year-old girl in West Sussex in 2016, all of which he denies.

Giving evidence behind a screen in the courtroom on Monday, Price said that she was told in texts between her and the alleged victim that Hayler "had tried to kiss her" and "had done stuff to her".

She added that when she confronted Hayler about the alleged rape, his "response all the time was 'no I hadn't'".

Asked further about what the girl had told her had happened, Price told jurors: "Definitely a kiss and that he said he loved her."

"I wanted to get information out of [the complainant] because it's serious," she added.

"I could tell that she was, like, afraid."

Price also told the jury that she had used Hayler's fingerprints while he was reportedly intoxicated to access his phone.

The trial previously heard that the alleged victim first contacted the NSPCC in 2021 over the allegations, who then referred her to the police, prompting the investigation.

Hayler was married to media personality Price at the time of the allegations, before the couple's relationship broke down in 2018 and they divorced in 2021.

Hayler has suggested his ex-wife "launched a campaign" against him when their marriage ended and the allegations form part of this, the court has heard.

The alleged victim is not part of Hayler or Price's extended families.

articles.title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs
articles.summary: Shabana Mahmood says there is "insufficient protection" for those who play a role in public life.
articles.body:
Political figures who are not currently MPs will be given police support, the home secretary has announced.

Shabana Mahmood told MPs there was "insufficient protection" for those serving in public life and that the new announcement will cover peers, former MPs and party spokespeople.

She also announced an urgent, independent review of security arrangements for high-profile figures including politicians and royals.

It comes three months after Reform UK spokeswoman and former Conservative MP Ann Widdecombe was found dead at her home in Devon, having been hit on the head with a hammer 21 times as she ate lunch.

Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged with her murder, and he was also charged with preparing acts of terror against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Kerry is alleged to have carried out research on prominent targets over a period of two years, including trying to gain entry into Farage's London home.

Speaking in the Commons on Monday, Mahmood said that "robust debate and criticism are part of this job - threats, abuse and violence are not."

She did not elaborate on what the support would involve, but told MPs it would include access to a named police officer and help with wider security measures.

The safety of politicians has been a prominent issue in recent years, following the murders of Conservative MP Sir David Amess in 2021 and Labour MP Jo Cox in 2016.

"We owe it to them and to everyone who believes in a fair and open country to ensure that those who serve at all levels receive the protection they deserve," Mahmood added.

The "root and branch" independent review into security arrangements will be led by former national security advisor Stephen Lovegrove, and will look into "physical threats, online risks and the dangers posed within our more polarised society".

Mahmood confirmed that the review will report within six months, and build on the existing work of Sir Robert Buckland, who is leading a separate review into the murder of Sir David.

In response, shadow home secretary Chris Philp welcomed the extension of protective measures, saying threats to elected representatives are threats to democracy.

Reform UK's home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf welcomed the review, but added: "It is disappointing that it took the murder of one of our colleagues, countless threats towards our party spokespeople and months of campaigning from Reform UK to make this government take action."

Reform has in recent months accused the government of a "dereliction of duty" over Farage's taxpayer-funded security, claiming it had previously been "downgraded" - a charge that the Home Office has said is "categorically untrue".

Decisions over the security of current MPs and members of the House of Lords are made by the House of Parliament's security team.

There is a separate, independent committee, the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (Ravec), to deal with high-profile political candidates, which is staffed by officials from the Home Office, the Cabinet Office, and the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

The Jo Cox Foundation welcomed the home secretary's announcement but said "strengthening physical security" alone was not enough.

"We must also tackle the root causes - including online harms and education - to prevent future attacks," its chief executive Olivia Field said in a statement on X.

According to data released to the BBC in April , the number of alleged offences against MPs have increased year-on-year, with 976 recorded in 2025, compared to 364 in 2019.

MPs reported 4,064 crimes to the Met's Parliamentary Liaison Team between 2019 and 2025. Most offences were related to malicious communications followed by harassment, and criminal damage to a building.

In 2025, there were 50 death threats reported - up from 31 the previous year.

articles.title: Zohran Mamdani orders use-of-force review for New York City police
articles.summary: City spokesperson says the mayor’s calls for reform are not connected to police response to an ICE shooting last week.
articles.body:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani has ordered a review of the New York City Police Department’s use of force for the first time in a decade amid renewed pressure from his progressive base for law enforcement reform.

On Monday, the city said it would introduce a “package of reforms” in addition to the review, to “strengthen accountability when police officers are accused of serious misconduct”.

The New York Police Department (NYPD) is the largest police force in the United States.

The reforms follow the retirement of a police officer involved in the shooting death of 19-year-old Win Rozario during a reported mental health crisis in 2024.

“That officer retired before a disciplinary trial could take place,” the mayor’s office said in a statement.

Among other measures Mamdani announced is $2.6m in additional funding for the Office of the Inspector General, which investigates NYPD policies and misconduct.

Monday’s statement also calls for a new notification system to ensure disciplinary hearings are completed before an officer retires, and it includes a renewed push for the department to comply with state-level reporting requirements about police-involved deaths.

The announcement comes amid pressure from Mamdani’s fellow progressives to enforce accountability at the city’s police department.

Much of the focus has fallen on a division within the NYPD called the Strategic Response Group, a rapid-response unit that addresses protests, major events and “civil disorder”.

Earlier this month, 17 state-level politicians and political nominees, including congressional candidates Claire Valdez and Darializa Avila Chevalier, called for the group to be disbanded. Both Valdez and Chevalier were endorsed by Mamdani.

In a statement, the politicians denounced the Strategic Response Group’s deployment during protests against a recent US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operation.

On October 8, an ICE officer shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgal while he was inside an SUV last week with his five-year-old son. The shooting, which took place in New York’s Marble Hill neighbourhood, sparked days of demonstrations against ICE’s tactics, as well as a police response.

Chevalier wrote in a post on social media that she was “shoved to the ground by an officer” during the protests. She also claimed to have observed other instances of excessive violence.

“When I was in Marble Hill last night I saw NYPD officers rapidly escalating violence,” Chevalier said.

“I witnessed unmarked law enforcement cars hitting protesters as NYPD officers pushed people out of its path.”

Mamdani condemned the shooting and called for Belgal’s release from federal custody.

Critics have frequently pointed to such incidents as examples of why greater police oversight is necessary.

Reported use of force within the NYPD has increased over the last decade, including physical force, the deployment of firearms, and the use of electrical weapons like tasers.

There were 12,348 reported use-of-force incidents in 2025, compared with 4,087 in 2016, when the department first started collecting such statistics.

Crime in New York City, however, has been on the downturn. Earlier this month, the city reported the “fewest shooting incidents, shooting victims, and murders” in the first nine months of the year and in the third quarter of the year, compared with any time in recorded history.

Major crime, which includes murder, rape, felony assault and grand larceny, declined 9.4 percent in the third quarter and 6.6 percent compared with the same period last year.

Still, Chevalier and other progressive politicians remained critical of the excess force authorised under the city’s police leadership. They have called on Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, who was originally appointed by Mamdani’s predecessor, Eric Adams, to step down.

The commissioner is appointed by the mayor. She can be removed either by the mayor or the governor of New York State.

According to recent reporting from The Atlantic magazine, New York State Governor Kathy Hochul made retaining Tisch as police commissioner a condition of her endorsement for Mamdani in the 2024 mayoral election.

In a statement to the magazine, Mamdani questioned that framing, saying Hochul’s support for keeping Tisch was “more of a recommendation” than a demand.

A New York City Hall spokesperson told Al Jazeera that the use-of-force review was already in the works prior to the October 8 ICE shooting and the protests that followed.

articles.title: How did Houthi missiles slip past Saudi defences? Riyadh probes deadly airport attack that killed 13
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia has launched an investigation into how its air defence systems failed to stop a barrage of missiles and drones fired by Iran-backed Houthi
articles.body: Saudi Arabia has launched an investigation into how its air defence systems failed to stop a barrage of missiles and drones fired by Iran-backed Houthi rebels at Riyadh, including a strike on King Khalid International Airport that killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300, two regional officials said on Monday. The probe will examine why the weapons reached the Saudi capital despite travelling more than 1,000 kilometres and why the military did not issue an earlier warning.The initial findings suggest the Houthis first launched multiple drones to pave the way for cruise and ballistic missiles to reach the airport, one of the officials said. The investigation is also examining why Saudi Arabia's air defence systems failed to intercept the incoming weapons.The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly. Saudi Arabia's government-run Center for International Communication, which oversees foreign media, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.The attack has raised serious questions about the kingdom's ability to defend its critical infrastructure as the conflict involving Iran and its regional allies spreads across the Middle East.Houthi attacks expose gaps in Saudi air defencesThe airport strike is among a series of Houthi attacks targeting Saudi airports since last week. The attacks have highlighted potential weaknesses in the kingdom's air defence network at a time when the wider regional conflict is intensifying.The Houthis possess ballistic missiles and advanced systems fitted with warheads that can change direction during flight. These weapons pose a challenge to Patriot interceptors and other air defence systems used by Saudi Arabia.The investigation will seek to establish how the missiles and drones travelled such a long distance without being intercepted or triggering an earlier warning.Saudi state-run media reported on Monday that the country's military was responding to another attack involving drones and cruise missiles. It did not provide further details.Riyadh airport remained closed on Monday. Workers in the capital's financial district were also told to work from home.Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman acknowledged the seriousness of the situation while addressing the World Petroleum Energy Congress in Riyadh.“The events of recent weeks are serious," he said. “Our response must be equally serious.”Saudi Arabia wants greater US involvement against HouthisSaudi Arabia wants the United States to play a more direct role in countering the Houthi attacks. Washington has provided intelligence sharing, target identification and planning support for a Saudi-led offensive, but has so far refrained from carrying out strikes against the rebels.US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he was considering military action against the Houthis following the deadly airport attack.However, a US intervention could widen the conflict and threaten a critical global shipping route. The Houthis could attempt to disrupt traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden near Yemen.Such a move could further restrict the movement of oil from the Persian Gulf. Global energy supplies are already facing disruption because of Iran's efforts to choke off the Strait of Hormuz, through which about one-fifth of the world's oil flowed before the US-Iran war began.The Houthis seized key areas along the Bab el-Mandeb last month. The Saudi-led coalition, which backs forces aligned with Yemen's internationally recognised government, has been trying to retake them.For Trump, the prospect of deeper military involvement comes at a politically sensitive time. The US midterm elections are approaching, and voters will decide whether his Republican Party retains control of Congress. Persistent inflation and high petrol prices, fuelled by the conflict with Iran, have contributed to widespread American disapproval of the war. A wider US military campaign in the region could add to that discontent.UAE calls for joint Gulf response as Iran offers mediationAnwar Gargash, a diplomatic adviser to the rulers of the United Arab Emirates, called on Monday for “joint Gulf action” to defend regional countries against attacks by Iran and its allied groups.Gargash said Iran and its allies had wrongly assumed that Gulf Arab states were “the weakest link” in the US war against Iran. Tehran and its allies have repeatedly attacked Arab countries across the Gulf during the conflict.“It has become clear that we are all targeted, and that our security is indivisible,” he wrote on social media.Iran's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, expressed concern over the fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis and offered to help resolve disputes.“We are severely concerned about developments in the Arabian Peninsula,” spokesman Esmail Baghaei said at his weekly briefing. “We have many times announced readiness for applying our good offices in order to facilitate talks between the two sides.”Baghaei said Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al-Saud spoke by phone on Sunday about the situation. He did not disclose further details of their conversation.Houthis report deaths in alleged Saudi strikes on YemenThe Houthi-run health ministry said on Monday that airstrikes on a government complex and a house in Yemen's northern al-Jawf province killed nine people, including five children and a woman. Seven others were wounded, according to the Houthi-controlled SABA news agency.Houthi officials also accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out fresh strikes on the Yemeni capital, Sanaa. They said the attacks killed one person and wounded 12.The claims could not be independently verified from the information available.The latest reports come as Saudi Arabia faces mounting pressure to protect its territory while supporting forces fighting the Houthis in Yemen.Jordanian killed in airport strike buried in AmmanMeanwhile, mourners gathered in Amman on Monday for the funeral of Mahmoud Al-Barqawi, a 33-year-old Jordanian killed in the missile strike on King Khalid International Airport.Al-Barqawi, who worked at a cafe in Riyadh and was the father of two children, was buried after a funeral procession began at a mosque in the Jordanian capital.His father, Hasan al-Barqawi, said the family was struggling to come to terms with the loss.“No one can truly feel the pain of this tragedy,” he said.The strike also wounded four Jordanian citizens. Jordan's Royal Court chief Yousef Al-Issawi attended the funeral and offered condolences on behalf of the king and crown prince.Despite the airport closure and the latest security concerns, Saudi Arabia continued with the second day of the World Petroleum Energy Congress in Riyadh on Monday.You use AI every day.
